Fact.Name: Had rental real estate or royalty income (Schedule E Part I)
Fact.Description: Interview gate. Schedule E instructions (2026 draft) printed p. 2 (PDF p. 3): "Use Schedule E (Form 1040) to report income or loss from rental real estate, royalties, ...". Gross income: 26 U.S.C. 61(a)(5), (a)(6).

Fact.Name: Has Schedule E Part I income
Fact.Description: True only when the gate is answered yes; false while unanswered so existing returns are unaffected.

Fact.Name: Rents received (Schedule E line 3, all properties)
Fact.Description: Instructions (2026 draft) printed p. 6 (PDF p. 7), Line 3: "If you received rental income from real estate (including personal property leased with real estate), report the income on line 3." 26 U.S.C. 61(a)(5).

Fact.Name: Rents received (Schedule E line 3, all properties) (derived)
Fact.Description: Rents received (Schedule E line 3, all properties), defaulting to $0 while unanswered so sums stay computable.

Fact.Name: Royalties received (Schedule E line 4, all properties)
Fact.Description: Instructions (2026 draft) printed p. 7 (PDF p. 8), Line 4: "Report on line 4 royalties from oil, gas, or mineral properties (not including operating interests); copyrights; ... and patents." 26 U.S.C. 61(a)(6).

Fact.Name: Royalties received (Schedule E line 4, all properties) (derived)
Fact.Description: Royalties received (Schedule E line 4, all properties), defaulting to $0 while unanswered so sums stay computable.

Fact.Name: Total expenses excluding depreciation (Schedule E lines 5-17 and 19, all properties)
Fact.Description: Schedule E line 20 total expenses, with line 18 (depreciation or depletion) always $0 in this slice because any depreciation is knocked out. Deductibility: 26 U.S.C. 212 (ordinary and necessary expenses for the production or collection of income / management of property held for the production of income).

Fact.Name: Total expenses excluding depreciation (Schedule E lines 5-17 and 19, all properties) (derived)
Fact.Description: Total expenses excluding depreciation (Schedule E lines 5-17 and 19, all properties), defaulting to $0 while unanswered so sums stay computable.

Fact.Name: Any single Part I property had a loss
Fact.Description: Asked because a loss on one property can be hidden by profit on another in the totals. Instructions (2026 draft) printed p. 9 (PDF p. 10), Line 22: "If you have a rental real estate loss from a passive activity (defined earlier), the amount of loss you can deduct may be limited by the passive activity loss rules. You may need to complete Form 8582". 26 U.S.C. 469; at-risk 465 (Line 21: "use Form 6198"); excess business loss 461(l) (Form 461).

Fact.Name: Claims depreciation, amortization, depletion, or vehicle expenses
Fact.Description: Instructions (2026 draft) printed p. 9 (PDF p. 10), Line 18: "See the Instructions for Form 4562 to figure the amount of depreciation to enter on line 18." Printed p. 8 (PDF p. 9): "If you claim any auto expenses (actual or the standard mileage rate), you must complete Part V of Form 4562". Form 4562 is not supported, so the TY2026 mileage rates (72.5 / 76 cents) and section 179 limits ($2,560,000 / $4,090,000) on printed p. 1 are not used.

Fact.Name: Any personal-use days at a rental dwelling unit
Fact.Description: Instructions (2026 draft) printed p. 6 (PDF p. 7), Line 2: "If you rented out a dwelling unit that you also used for personal purposes during the year, you may not be able to deduct all the expenses for the rental part." 26 U.S.C. 280A(c)(5), (e): expense allocation / limits when the unit is used as a residence: https://www.law.cornell.edu/uscode/text/26/280A

Fact.Name: Provides substantial services to renters (cleaning, linens, maid service)
Fact.Description: Instructions for Schedule E (2026 draft) printed p. 7 (PDF p. 8), Line 3: "Generally, rental real estate activity is reported on Schedule E even if it is also a trade or business activity; however, if you provided significant services to the renter, such as maid service, report the rental activity on Schedule C, not on Schedule E. Significant services do not include the furnishing of heat and light, cleaning of public areas, trash collection, or similar services." On Schedule C the profit can be subject to self-employment tax (26 U.S.C. 1401). 26 U.S.C. 1402(a)(1) excludes "rentals from real estate" from net earnings from self-employment; the Schedule C routing above is what takes substantial-service rentals out of that exclusion, so reporting the profit here with $0 SE tax could understate tax.

Fact.Name: Has partnership, S corporation, estate, trust, or REMIC income (Schedule E Parts II-IV)
Fact.Description: Parts II-IV (K-1 income) are out of scope for this MVP (spec PR #8, item 4: "block with clear message").

Fact.Name: Any Part I rental is a trade or business (26 U.S.C. 199A)
Fact.Description: #185: a rental that is a trade or business produces qualified business income for the 26 U.S.C. 199A deduction (https://www.law.cornell.edu/uscode/text/26/199A). 26 CFR 1.199A-1(b)(14) (https://www.law.cornell.edu/cfr/text/26/1.199A-1): "Trade or business means a trade or business that is a trade or business under section 162 (a section 162 trade or business) other than the trade or business of performing services as an employee. In addition, rental or licensing of tangible or intangible property (rental activity) that does not rise to the level of a section 162 trade or business is nevertheless treated as a trade or business for purposes of section 199A, if the property is rented or licensed to a trade or business conducted by the individual or an RPE which is commonly controlled". Rev. Proc. 2019-38 (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-drop/rp-19-38.pdf) gives a safe harbor for a rental real estate enterprise with 250 or more hours of rental services a year.

Fact.Name: Schedule E Part I total income or (loss) (line 26 / line 41 to Schedule 1 line 5)
Fact.Description: Line 21 per property = (line 3 rents and/or line 4 royalties) - line 20 total expenses; line 26 combines them. Schedule E (2026) draft p. 1, line 21: "Subtract line 20 from line 3 (rents) and/or 4 (royalties)"; line 26: "Total rental real estate and royalty income or (loss). ... Schedule 1 (Form 1040), line 5." Because every loss is knocked out, lines 22 and 25 (passive-loss limits) are always zero here. $0 when the gate is unanswered or no.

Fact.Name: Knockout: Schedule E rental or royalty loss
Fact.Description: Any net loss (total or on any one property) is unsupported: passive activity loss limits (26 U.S.C. 469, Form 8582), at-risk limits (26 U.S.C. 465, Form 6198), and excess business loss (26 U.S.C. 461(l), Form 461). Cites on /scheduleEAnyPropertyLoss.

Fact.Name: Knockout: Schedule E depreciation or vehicle expenses (Form 4562)
Fact.Description: Form 4562 is not supported. Cites on /scheduleEHasDepreciation.

Fact.Name: Knockout: personal use of a rental dwelling unit (IRC 280A)
Fact.Description: Expense allocation under 26 U.S.C. 280A is not supported. Cites on /scheduleEHasPersonalUse.

Fact.Name: Knockout: rental with substantial services (belongs on Schedule C with SE tax)
Fact.Description: Belongs on Schedule C and is subject to SE tax, not Schedule E. Cites on /scheduleEProvidesSubstantialServices.

Fact.Name: Knockout: Schedule E Parts II-IV (K-1) income
Fact.Description: Partnership / S corporation / estate / trust / REMIC income is not supported in this MVP.

Fact.Name: Knockout: Schedule E rental treated as a trade or business (QBI not computed)
Fact.Description: #185: a trade-or-business rental needs the 26 U.S.C. 199A deduction on Form 1040 (2026) draft line 13b, "Qualified business income deduction from Form 8995 or Form 8995-A" (PDF p. 3). Line 13b (taxCalculations /qualifiedBusinessIncomeDeduction) is not computed yet, so a "yes" is stopped instead of filing line 13b as $0. Cites on /scheduleERentalIsTradeOrBusiness. Complete false when there is no Part I income (/hasScheduleEIncome false) or the answer is "no"; incomplete while a filer with Part I income has not answered, and /scheduleESectionIsComplete requires the answer.

Fact.Name: Knockout: Schedule E income with the EITC
Fact.Description: 26 U.S.C. 32(i)(2)(C): disqualified income includes "the excess (if any) of— (i) gross income from rents or royalties not derived in the ordinary course of a trade or business, over (ii) the sum of" the allocable deductions. The eitc modules do not include Schedule E in the investment-income test yet, so any nonzero Schedule E result with EITC eligibility is knocked out. https://www.law.cornell.edu/uscode/text/26/32

Fact.Name: Schedule E section complete
Fact.Description: Gate answered; if yes, every amount and screener question answered.
